````text
I'll now provide a comprehensive read-only report of the build-ai-index-ts.mjs architecture and extension points.

## Report: build-ai-index-ts.mjs Inspection

### 1. ts-morph Project Configuration

**Project Build (Line 348):**
```
const project = new Project({ tsConfigFilePath: TSCONFIG, skipAddingFilesFromTsConfig: true });
```

- **TSCONFIG path:** `ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/tsconfig.json` (line 24)
  - Resolves jimu-* modules via `paths` aliases
  - Includes: `dist/widgets`, `your-extensions`, `types`, node_modules/@esri types
- **Skip auto-include:** `skipAddingFilesFromTsConfig: true` - explicit glob control instead of tsconfig includes

**Source Roots & File Selection (Lines 349-354):**
```
const globs = [];
for (const group of groups) {
  globs.push(`${WIDGETS_GLOB}/${group}/**/*.ts`, `${WIDGETS_GLOB}/${group}/**/*.tsx`);
}
globs.push(`!${WIDGETS_GLOB}/**/{i18n,t9n,nls,translations}/**`, `!${WIDGETS_GLOB}/**/*.{i18n,t9n}.*`);
```

- **Source root:** `ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/dist/widgets` (absolute at line 23)
- **Glob pattern:** Per-group traversal under `dist/widgets/<group>/**/*.{ts,tsx}`
- **Exclusions:** i18n/t9n/nls/translations directories and `.i18n`/`.t9n` named files
  - Enforced at line 31-34 (`isLocale()`) and line 143 (`isLocale()`)

### 2. Output Ownership & Cleanup

**Line 343-344 - Aggressive Cleanup:**
```
await fs.rm(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true, force: true });
await fs.mkdir(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
```

- **OUT_DIR:** `.ai-context/exb/dist-widgets-ts` (line 20)
- **Policy:** Complete removal + fresh directory per run
- **No preserved outputs** (unlike `build-ai-index.mjs`, which reserves 'api', 'api-usage', 'dist-widgets-ts', etc.)
  - This script owns the entire `dist-widgets-ts/` tree exclusively

### 3. Reusable Helpers & Main Phases

**Main Phases:**

| Phase | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **Setup** | 335-347 | Read widget groups, prepare output dir |
| **Project Load** | 348-354 | Create ts-morph Project, add source files via glob |
| **File Extraction** | 356-367 | Iterate SourceFiles, call `extractFile()` per file |
| **Output Write** | 369-381 | Write 10 TSV files + README |

**Reusable Helpers:**

| Helper | Lines | Signature | Purpose |
|--------|-------|-----------|---------|
| `clean(s, max=200)` | 289-293 | String → String | Normalize whitespace, strip dynamic imports, truncate |
| `safe(fn)` | 294-296 | Fn → Result\|'' | Catch exceptions, return empty string on failure |
| `typeOf(node, max)` | 297 | Node → String | Extract resolved type text from ts-morph node |
| `paramText(node)` | 298-307 | Function → String | Format parameters with names and types (e.g., `x?: number, y: string`) |
| `jsdocOf(node)` | 308-310 | Node → String | Extract JSDoc description text |
| `returnsJSX(fnLike)` | 311-313 | Function → Boolean | Detect JSX return type via regex on resolved type text |
| `firstGeneric(typeText)` | 314-317 | String → String | Extract first generic type arg (e.g., `<T>` from `Array<T>`) |
| `pushProps(compName, propsType, atNode, ctx)` | 100-125 | Void | Emit component prop rows; per-prop type + JSDoc |
| `relOf(sf)` | 71 | SourceFile → String | Convert absolute path to workspace-relative (forward slashes) |
| `widgetOf(rel)` | 75-79 | String → {group, widget} | Parse group/widget from dist/widgets path segment |

**Core Extraction Function (`extractFile()` at line 127+):**
- Iterates SourceFile AST: functions, variables (arrow/HOC forms), classes, interfaces, type aliases, enums
- Per each, detects: exported status, arity (function/component/hook), form (arrow/memo/forwardRef/fc/class)
- Builds: symbols.tsv, functions.tsv, hooks.tsv, components.tsv, classes.tsv, methods.tsv, fields.tsv
- Aggregates imports per module with **resolved target file** (line 304 `getModuleSpecifierSourceFile()`)
- Captures re-exports (line 315-327)
- Component props extraction via `pushProps()`: per component, emit up to 60 prop rows with type + JSDoc

### 4. Extension Point for Phase 1 Canonical API Tables (Lines 82-96 of session plan)

**Smallest Grounded Extension Point: After TSV Output (Post-Line 381)**

The Phase 1 requirements are:
- `symbols.tsv` → **one row per stable identity** (api_id-based, not name-based)
- `declarations.tsv` → per overload/merge, with location and containing symbol
- `exports.tsv` → per verified export, with canonical flag
- `relations.tsv` → declaration graph (extends/implements/type-alias-target/member-type)
- `METADATA.tsv` → centralized schema/provenance

**Proposed extension** (pseudocode location):
```javascript
// After writeTsv(...reexports.tsv) at line 380:

// Phase 1: Build normalized canonical API tables
const phase1 = buildPhase1(out, project);
await writeTsv(path.join(OUT_DIR, 'api', 'symbols.tsv'), 
  'api_id\tpackage\tmodule_path\tname\tkind\tparent_api_id\tmember_name\tstatic\toptional\taccessibility\tvisibility\tmatch_status\tdeprecated\tdeprecation_message',
  phase1.symbols);
// ... emit declarations.tsv, exports.tsv, relations.tsv, METADATA.tsv
```

**New Functions Required:**

1. **`buildSymbolIdentities(out, project)`** - Build stable ID mapping:
   - For each row in `out.symbols`, create `api_id` = deterministic path-qualified ID
   - Track parent (class name for methods, interface name for fields)
   - Assign visibility (public-documented, public-declared-undocumented, internal-tagged, not-exported, implementation-private, unknown)

2. **`collectDeclarations(project)`** - Multideclaration tracking:
   - Per api_id, iterate `node.getDeclarations()` (all, not just [0])
   - Track overload_index and merge_index
   - Emit locations (path, start_line, start_column, end_line, end_column)

3. **`resolveExports(project, symbols)`** - Export canonicalization:
   - For each symbol, find all re-export paths
   - Determine canonical export (docs + Storybook + public barrel = highest weight)

4. **`buildRelationGraph(project, symbols)`** - Declaration relations:
   - Track `extends` links (class → parent)
   - Track `implements` links (class → interface)
   - Track type-alias targets
   - Track member types (property/method return types as potential relations)

### 5. Risks: Declaration/Source Duplicate Identities & Exports

**A. Multideclaration Pluralism**

- **Issue:** `sym.getDeclarations()` returns ALL declarations for a symbol (line 112)
  - Merged interfaces: `interface Foo { a: 1 }` + `interface Foo { b: 2 }`
  - Overloaded functions: multiple `function foo(...)`
  - The script only uses `[0]` (first) - loses merge/overload evidence
- **Phase 1 risk:** Must emit `declarations.tsv` with overload_index and merge_index to avoid collapsing polymorphism
- **Mitigation:** In Phase 1 builder, iterate ALL declarations per api_id; assign indices deterministically

**B. Export Ambiguity (No Canonical Marker)**

- **Issue:** `reexports.tsv` (line 315-327) captures that a symbol is re-exported but does NOT mark which export is canonical
  - Example: `export { WidgetManager }` from index.ts (source), ALSO `export { WidgetManager }` from public-api.ts (barrel)
  - Phase 1 `exports.tsv` requires a `canonical` flag per plan line 89
- **Current limitation:** build-ai-index-ts.mjs only emits re-exports (which module re-exports it), not export list per symbol
- **Mitigation:** Phase 1 must:
  1. Correlate `reexports.tsv` + symbol location to build export manifest
  2. Cross-reference with docs (ArcGIS Experience Builder API reference) + Storybook manifest presence
  3. Mark canonical = true if: documented OR (Storybook entry AND public barrel) OR (only export path)

**C. Import Resolution Ambiguity (.d.ts vs .ts)**

- **Issue:** Line 304 `getModuleSpecifierSourceFile()` resolves imports to their target file
  - Could resolve to `.d.ts` (declaration) OR `.ts` (source)
  - TypeScript prefers .d.ts if both exist
- **Phase 1 risk:** Exports.tsv must disambiguate source_path (did it come from source or declaration?)
- **Mitigation:** In Phase 1 export resolver, check if resolved file is `.d.ts` vs `.ts`; prefer source when tracking origin

**D. Accessor Proliferation (Getter/Setter Collapse)**

- **Issue:** Properties with accessors may emit as separate getter/setter nodes
  - `cls.getProperties()` might yield both `foo` (property) and separate `get foo()`/`set foo()`
  - Potential for name collisions in identity mapping
- **Phase 1 risk:** Stable ID must collapse getter/setter into single api_id with member_kind = property|getter|setter
- **Mitigation:** During identity building, merge getters and setters under a single property api_id

**E. Path-Qualified Local Symbol Identity**

- **Issue:** Non-exported symbols in different files share the same name
  - `utils/componentA.tsx` has local `const foo = ...`
  - `utils/componentB.tsx` has local `const foo = ...`
  - Naive ID = "foo" collides
- **Current script:** Uses only exported symbols for the main index (line 174-175: `if (exported === 'export' || callable)`)
- **Phase 1 risk:** For implementation-private visibility, must use path-qualified ID: `ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/dist/widgets/arcgis/map/lib/utils/componentA.tsx::foo`
- **Mitigation:** Enforce path-qualified IDs for non-exported symbols in Phase 1 identity building

---

**Summary Tables:**

| Component | Location | Reusability |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Locale exclusion logic | Lines 31-34, 143 | **High** - regex patterns and helper functions portable |
| Type extraction + safe unwrap | Lines 297-313 | **High** - directly reusable in Phase 1 type inference |
| Import aggregation + resolution | Lines 285-312 | **High** - import grouping by module + resolved target is core |
| Per-file AST walk | Line 127-327 | **Medium** - extractFile() is specialized; inner loops reusable |
| Component form detection | Lines 178-218 | **Medium** - pattern matching for arrow/memo/fc/class; needs Phase 1 enhancement for stable form |
````

The catalog pass will load Jimu declarations into the same project, derive public identities from actual entrypoint exports, keep private/local IDs path-qualified, and write `api/` separately from the existing widget tables.

````text
### Get Exported Declarations from File

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/exports.md

Retrieve all exported declarations from a file or module using `getExportedDeclarations()`. This returns a map where keys are export names and values are the corresponding declarations.

```typescript
// main.ts
export * from "./classes";
export { Interface1 as AliasedInterface } from "./interfaces";

namespace MergedNamespace { let t; }
namespace MergedNamespace { let u; }

export { MergedNamespace };

export default 5;

// classes.ts
export * from "./Class1";
export * from "./Class2";

// Class1.ts
export class Class1 {}

// Class2.ts
export class Class2 {}

// interfaces.ts
export interface Interface1 {}
export interface Interface2 {}
```

```typescript
import { ExportedDeclarations, Project } from "ts-morph";

const project = new Project();
project.addSourceFilesAtPaths("**/*.ts");
const mainFile = project.getSourceFileOrThrow("main.ts");

for (const [name, declarations] of mainFile.getExportedDeclarations())
  console.log(`${name}: ${declarations.map(d => d.getText()).join(", ")}`);
```

```typescript
Class1: export class Class1 {}
Class2: export class Class2 {}
AliasedInterface: export interface Interface1 {}
MergedNamespace: namespace MergedNamespace { let t; }, namespace MergedNamespace { let u; }
default: 5
```

--------------------------------

### Get Module Declaration Kind

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/modules.md

Check the declaration kind of a module declaration.

```typescript
moduleDeclaration.getDeclarationKind(); // returns: ModuleDeclarationKind
```

--------------------------------

### Navigate and Query AST with ts-morph

Source: https://context7.com/dsherret/ts-morph/llms.txt

Use ts-morph to navigate and query the Abstract Syntax Tree to find and analyze code elements. This includes getting specific declarations by type or name, filtering by conditions, and navigating relationships between code elements.

```typescript
import { Project, SyntaxKind, Node } from "ts-morph";

const project = new Project();
const sourceFile = project.createSourceFile("navigation.ts", `
interface Person {
  name: string;
  age: number;
}

class Employee implements Person {
  constructor(public name: string, public age: number) {}

  greet(): string {
    return `Hello, ${this.name}`;
  }
}

export default Employee;
`);

// Get specific declarations
const interfaces = sourceFile.getInterfaces();
const classes = sourceFile.getClasses();
const functions = sourceFile.getFunctions();
const enums = sourceFile.getEnums();
const typeAliases = sourceFile.getTypeAliases();

// Get by name
const personInterface = sourceFile.getInterface("Person");
const employeeClass = sourceFile.getClass("Employee");

// Get by condition
const classWithConstructor = sourceFile.getClass(c => c.getConstructors().length > 0);
const interfaceWithTwoProps = sourceFile.getInterface(i => i.getProperties().length === 2);

// Navigate relationships
if (employeeClass) {
  // Get implements
  const implements_ = employeeClass.getImplements();

  // Get base class
  const baseClass = employeeClass.getBaseClass();

  // Get derived classes
  const derivedClasses = employeeClass.getDerivedClasses();

  // Get members
  const methods = employeeClass.getMethods();
  const properties = employeeClass.getProperties();
  const constructors = employeeClass.getConstructors();
}

// Find descendants by kind
const allIdentifiers = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.Identifier);
const allStringLiterals = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.StringLiteral);

// Check node types
const firstClass = classes[0];
if (Node.isClassDeclaration(firstClass)) {
  // TypeScript knows this is a ClassDeclaration
  console.log(firstClass.getName());
}

// Get referencing and referenced files
const referencingFiles = sourceFile.getReferencingSourceFiles();
const referencedFiles = sourceFile.getReferencedSourceFiles();
const importStringLiterals = sourceFile.getImportStringLiterals();
```

--------------------------------

### Get Static Properties

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/classes.md

Retrieve static properties declared in a class. You can get all static properties, a specific static property by name, or the first static property matching a condition.

```typescript
const staticProperties = classDeclaration.getStaticProperties();
const myStaticProperty = classDeclaration.getStaticProperty("myStaticProperty");
const myStaticStringProperty = classDeclaration.getStaticProperty(p =>
    Node.isPropertyDeclaration(p) && p.getType().getText() === "string");
```

### Class Declaration Methods > Get members

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/classes.md

You can retrieve all members of a class declaration, including both static and instance members, by using the `getMembers()` method. For instance members specifically, use `getInstanceMembers()`, and for static members, use `getStaticMembers()`.
````

````text
## Report: build-ai-index-ts.mjs Inspection

### 1. ts-morph Project Configuration

**Project Build (Line 348):**

- **Skip auto-include:** `skipAddingFilesFromTsConfig: true` - explicit glob control instead of tsconfig includes

**Source Roots & File Selection (Lines 349-354):**
```
const globs = [];
for (const group of groups) {
  globs.push(`${WIDGETS_GLOB}/${group}/**/*.ts`, `${WIDGETS_GLOB}/${group}/**/*.tsx`);
}
globs.push(`!${WIDGETS_GLOB}/**/{i18n,t9n,nls,translations}/**`, `!${WIDGETS_GLOB}/**/*.{i18n,t9n}.*`);
```

- **Source root:** `ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/dist/widgets` (absolute at line 23)
- **Glob pattern:** Per-group traversal under `dist/widgets/<group>/**/*.{ts,tsx}`
- **Exclusions:** i18n/t9n/nls/translations directories and `.i18n`/`.t9n` named files
  - Enforced at line 31-34 (`isLocale()`) and line 143 (`isLocale()`)

### 2. Output Ownership & Cleanup

**Line 343-344 - Aggressive Cleanup:**
```

await fs.mkdir(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
```

- **OUT_DIR:** `.ai-context/exb/dist-widgets-ts` (line 20)
- **Policy:** Complete removal + fresh directory per run
- **No preserved outputs** (unlike `build-ai-index.mjs`, which reserves 'api', 'api-usage', 'dist-widgets-ts', etc.)
  - This script owns the entire `dist-widgets-ts/` tree exclusively

### 3. Reusable Helpers & Main Phases

**Main Phases:**

| Phase | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **Setup** | 335-347 | Read widget groups, prepare output dir |
| **Project Load** | 348-354 | Create ts-morph Project, add source files via glob |
| **File Extraction** | 356-367 | Iterate SourceFiles, call `extractFile()` per file |
| **Output Write** | 369-381 | Write 10 TSV files + README |

**Reusable Helpers:**

| Helper | Lines | Signature | Purpose |
|--------|-------|-----------|---------|
| `clean(s, max=200)` | 289-293 | String → String | Normalize whitespace, strip dynamic imports, truncate |
| `safe(fn)` | 294-296 | Fn → Result\|'' | Catch exceptions, return empty string on failure |
| `typeOf(node, max)` | 297 | Node → String | Extract resolved type text from ts-morph node |
| `paramText(node)` | 298-307 | Function → String | Format parameters with names and types (e.g., `x?: number, y: string`) |
| `jsdocOf(node)` | 308-310 | Node → String | Extract JSDoc description text |
| `returnsJSX(fnLike)` | 311-313 | Function → Boolean | Detect JSX return type via regex on resolved type text |
| `firstGeneric(typeText)` | 314-317 | String → String | Extract first generic type arg (e.g., `<T>` from `Array<T>`) |
| `pushProps(compName, propsType, atNode, ctx)` | 100-125 | Void | Emit component prop rows; per-prop type + JSDoc |
| `relOf(sf)` | 71 | SourceFile → String | Convert absolute path to workspace-relative (forward slashes) |
| `widgetOf(rel)` | 75-79 | String → {group, widget} | Parse group/widget from dist/widgets path segment |

**Core Extraction Function (`extractFile()` at line 127+):**
- Iterates SourceFile AST: functions, variables (arrow/HOC forms), classes, interfaces, type aliases, enums
- Per each, detects: exported status, arity (function/component/hook), form (arrow/memo/forwardRef/fc/class)
- Builds: symbols.tsv, functions.tsv, hooks.tsv, components.tsv, classes.tsv, methods.tsv, fields.tsv
- Aggregates imports per module with **resolved target file** (line 304 `getModuleSpecifierSourceFile()`)
- Captures re-exports (line 315-327)
- Component props extraction via `pushProps()`: per component, emit up to 60 prop rows with type + JSDoc

### 4. Extension Point for Phase 1 Canonical API Tables (Lines 82-96 of session plan)

**Smallest Grounded Extension Point: After TSV Output (Post-Line 381)**

The Phase 1 requirements are:
- `symbols.tsv` → **one row per stable identity** (api_id-based, not name-based)
- `declarations.tsv` → per overload/merge, with location and containing symbol
- `exports.tsv` → per verified export, with canonical flag
- `relations.tsv` → declaration graph (extends/implements/type-alias-target/member-type)
- `METADATA.tsv` → centralized schema/provenance

**Proposed extension** (pseudocode location):
```javascript
// After writeTsv(...reexports.tsv) at line 380:

// Phase 1: Build normalized canonical API tables
const phase1 = buildPhase1(out, project);
await writeTsv(path.join(OUT_DIR, 'api', 'symbols.tsv'), 
  'api_id\tpackage\tmodule_path\tname\tkind\tparent_api_id\tmember_name\tstatic\toptional\taccessibility\tvisibility\tmatch_status\tdeprecated\tdeprecation_message',
  phase1.symbols);
// ... emit declarations.tsv, exports.tsv, relations.tsv, METADATA.tsv
```

**New Functions Required:**

1. **`buildSymbolIdentities(out, project)`** - Build stable ID mapping:
   - For each row in `out.symbols`, create `api_id` = deterministic path-qualified ID
   - Track parent (class name for methods, interface name for fields)
   - Assign visibility (public-documented, public-declared-undocumented, internal-tagged, not-exported, implementation-private, unknown)

2. **`collectDeclarations(project)`** - Multideclaration tracking:
   - Per api_id, iterate `node.getDeclarations()` (all, not just [0])
   - Track overload_index and merge_index
   - Emit locations (path, start_line, start_column, end_line, end_column)

3. **`resolveExports(project, symbols)`** - Export canonicalization:
   - For each symbol, find all re-export paths
   - Determine canonical export (docs + Storybook + public barrel = highest weight)

4. **`buildRelationGraph(project, symbols)`** - Declaration relations:
   - Track `extends` links (class → parent)
   - Track `implements` links (class → interface)
   - Track type-alias targets
   - Track member types (property/method return types as potential relations)

### 5. Risks: Declaration/Source Duplicate Identities & Exports

**A. Multideclaration Pluralism**

- **Issue:** `sym.getDeclarations()` returns ALL declarations for a symbol (line 112)
  - Merged interfaces: `interface Foo { a: 1 }` + `interface Foo { b: 2 }`
  - Overloaded functions: multiple `function foo(...)`
  - The script only uses `[0]` (first) - loses merge/overload evidence
- **Phase 1 risk:** Must emit `declarations.tsv` with overload_index and merge_index to avoid collapsing polymorphism
- **Mitigation:** In Phase 1 builder, iterate ALL declarations per api_id; assign indices deterministically

**B. Export Ambiguity (No Canonical Marker)**

- **Issue:** `reexports.tsv` (line 315-327) captures that a symbol is re-exported but does NOT mark which export is canonical
  - Example: `export { WidgetManager }` from index.ts (source), ALSO `export { WidgetManager }` from public-api.ts (barrel)
  - Phase 1 `exports.tsv` requires a `canonical` flag per plan line 89
- **Current limitation:** build-ai-index-ts.mjs only emits re-exports (which module re-exports it), not export list per symbol
- **Mitigation:** Phase 1 must:
  1. Correlate `reexports.tsv` + symbol location to build export manifest
  2. Cross-reference with docs (ArcGIS Experience Builder API reference) + Storybook manifest presence
  3. Mark canonical = true if: documented OR (Storybook entry AND public barrel) OR (only export path)

**C. Import Resolution Ambiguity (.d.ts vs .ts)**

- **Issue:** Line 304 `getModuleSpecifierSourceFile()` resolves imports to their target file
  - Could resolve to `.d.ts` (declaration) OR `.ts` (source)
  - TypeScript prefers .d.ts if both exist
- **Phase 1 risk:** Exports.tsv must disambiguate source_path (did it come from source or declaration?)
- **Mitigation:** In Phase 1 export resolver, check if resolved file is `.d.ts` vs `.ts`; prefer source when tracking origin

**D. Accessor Proliferation (Getter/Setter Collapse)**

- **Issue:** Properties with accessors may emit as separate getter/setter nodes
  - `cls.getProperties()` might yield both `foo` (property) and separate `get foo()`/`set foo()`
  - Potential for name collisions in identity mapping
- **Phase 1 risk:** Stable ID must collapse getter/setter into single api_id with member_kind = property|getter|setter
- **Mitigation:** During identity building, merge getters and setters under a single property api_id

**E. Path-Qualified Local Symbol Identity**

- **Issue:** Non-exported symbols in different files share the same name
  - `utils/componentA.tsx` has local `const foo = ...`
  - `utils/componentB.tsx` has local `const foo = ...`
  - Naive ID = "foo" collides
- **Current script:** Uses only exported symbols for the main index (line 174-175: `if (exported === 'export' || callable)`)
- **Phase 1 risk:** For implementation-private visibility, must use path-qualified ID: `ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/dist/widgets/arcgis/map/lib/utils/componentA.tsx::foo`
- **Mitigation:** Enforce path-qualified IDs for non-exported symbols in Phase 1 identity building

---

**Summary Tables:**

| Component | Location | Reusability |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Locale exclusion logic | Lines 31-34, 143 | **High** - regex patterns and helper functions portable |
| Type extraction + safe unwrap | Lines 297-313 | **High** - directly reusable in Phase 1 type inference |
| Import aggregation + resolution | Lines 285-312 | **High** - import grouping by module + resolved target is core |
| Per-file AST walk | Line 127-327 | **Medium** - extractFile() is specialized; inner loops reusable |
| Component form detection | Lines 178-218 | **Medium** - pattern matching for arrow/memo/fc/class; needs Phase 1 enhancement for stable form |
````

````text
### Get Exported Declarations from File

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/exports.md

Retrieve all exported declarations from a file or module using `getExportedDeclarations()`. This returns a map where keys are export names and values are the corresponding declarations.

```typescript
// main.ts
export * from "./classes";
export { Interface1 as AliasedInterface } from "./interfaces";

namespace MergedNamespace { let t; }
namespace MergedNamespace { let u; }

export { MergedNamespace };

export default 5;

// classes.ts
export * from "./Class1";
export * from "./Class2";

// Class1.ts
export class Class1 {}

// Class2.ts
export class Class2 {}

// interfaces.ts
export interface Interface1 {}
export interface Interface2 {}
```

```typescript
import { ExportedDeclarations, Project } from "ts-morph";

const project = new Project();
project.addSourceFilesAtPaths("**/*.ts");
const mainFile = project.getSourceFileOrThrow("main.ts");

for (const [name, declarations] of mainFile.getExportedDeclarations())
  console.log(`${name}: ${declarations.map(d => d.getText()).join(", ")}`);
```

```typescript
Class1: export class Class1 {}
Class2: export class Class2 {}
AliasedInterface: export interface Interface1 {}
MergedNamespace: namespace MergedNamespace { let t; }, namespace MergedNamespace { let u; }
default: 5
```

--------------------------------

### Get Module Declaration Kind

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/modules.md

Check the declaration kind of a module declaration.

```typescript
moduleDeclaration.getDeclarationKind(); // returns: ModuleDeclarationKind
```

--------------------------------

### Navigate and Query AST with ts-morph

Source: https://context7.com/dsherret/ts-morph/llms.txt

Use ts-morph to navigate and query the Abstract Syntax Tree to find and analyze code elements. This includes getting specific declarations by type or name, filtering by conditions, and navigating relationships between code elements.

```typescript
import { Project, SyntaxKind, Node } from "ts-morph";

const project = new Project();
const sourceFile = project.createSourceFile("navigation.ts", `
interface Person {
  name: string;
  age: number;
}

class Employee implements Person {
  constructor(public name: string, public age: number) {}

  greet(): string {
    return `Hello, ${this.name}`;
  }
}

export default Employee;
`);

// Get specific declarations
const interfaces = sourceFile.getInterfaces();
const classes = sourceFile.getClasses();
const functions = sourceFile.getFunctions();
const enums = sourceFile.getEnums();
const typeAliases = sourceFile.getTypeAliases();

// Get by name
const personInterface = sourceFile.getInterface("Person");
const employeeClass = sourceFile.getClass("Employee");

// Get by condition
const classWithConstructor = sourceFile.getClass(c => c.getConstructors().length > 0);
const interfaceWithTwoProps = sourceFile.getInterface(i => i.getProperties().length === 2);

// Navigate relationships
if (employeeClass) {
  // Get implements
  const implements_ = employeeClass.getImplements();

  // Get base class
  const baseClass = employeeClass.getBaseClass();

  // Get derived classes
  const derivedClasses = employeeClass.getDerivedClasses();

  // Get members
  const methods = employeeClass.getMethods();
  const properties = employeeClass.getProperties();
  const constructors = employeeClass.getConstructors();
}

// Find descendants by kind
const allIdentifiers = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.Identifier);
const allStringLiterals = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.StringLiteral);

// Check node types
const firstClass = classes[0];
if (Node.isClassDeclaration(firstClass)) {
  // TypeScript knows this is a ClassDeclaration
  console.log(firstClass.getName());
}

// Get referencing and referenced files
const referencingFiles = sourceFile.getReferencingSourceFiles();
const referencedFiles = sourceFile.getReferencedSourceFiles();
const importStringLiterals = sourceFile.getImportStringLiterals();
```

--------------------------------

### Get Static Properties

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/classes.md

Retrieve static properties declared in a class. You can get all static properties, a specific static property by name, or the first static property matching a condition.

```typescript
const staticProperties = classDeclaration.getStaticProperties();
const myStaticProperty = classDeclaration.getStaticProperty("myStaticProperty");
const myStaticStringProperty = classDeclaration.getStaticProperty(p =>
    Node.isPropertyDeclaration(p) && p.getType().getText() === "string");
```

### Class Declaration Methods > Get members

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/classes.md

You can retrieve all members of a class declaration, including both static and instance members, by using the `getMembers()` method. For instance members specifically, use `getInstanceMembers()`, and for static members, use `getStaticMembers()`.
````

````text
### Access Underlying Compiler Node

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/navigation/compiler-nodes.md

Get the underlying TypeScript compiler node from a ts-morph node object. Warning: Do not hold onto these nodes between AST manipulations as they can become outdated.

```typescript
const compilerNode = interfaceDeclaration.compilerNode;
```

--------------------------------

### getAncestors and getParent

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/packages/ts-morph/src/compiler/ast/common/Node.ts

getAncestors walks up the tree yielding all parents in ascending order. getParent retrieves the direct parent from the compiler node. Together they let you traverse the AST upward.

```typescript
  /**
   * Goes up the tree getting all the parents in ascending order.
   */
  getAncestors(): Node[];
  /**
   * @internal - This is internal for now. I'm not sure what the correct behaviour should be.
   */
  getAncestors(includeSyntaxLists: boolean): Node[];
  getAncestors(includeSyntaxLists = false) {
    return Array.from(this._getAncestorsIterator(includeSyntaxLists));
  }

  /**
   * @internal
   */
  *_getAncestorsIterator(includeSyntaxLists: boolean): IterableIterator<Node> {
    let parent = getParent(this);
    while (parent != null) {
      yield parent;
      parent = getParent(parent!);
    }

    function getParent(node: Node) {
      return includeSyntaxLists ? node.getParentSyntaxList() || node.getParent() : node.getParent();
    }
  }

  /**
   * Get the node's parent.
   */
  getParent() {
    return this._getNodeFromCompilerNodeIfExists(this.compilerNode.parent);
  }

  /**
   * Gets the parent or throws an error if it doesn't exist.
   */
  getParentOrThrow(message?: string | (() => string)) {
    return errors.throwIfNullOrUndefined(this.getParent(), message ?? "Expected to find a parent.", this);
  }
```

--------------------------------

### Navigate and Query AST with ts-morph

Source: https://context7.com/dsherret/ts-morph/llms.txt

Use ts-morph to navigate and query the Abstract Syntax Tree to find and analyze code elements. This includes getting specific declarations by type or name, filtering by conditions, and navigating relationships between code elements.

```typescript
import { Project, SyntaxKind, Node } from "ts-morph";

const project = new Project();
const sourceFile = project.createSourceFile("navigation.ts", `
interface Person {
  name: string;
  age: number;
}

class Employee implements Person {
  constructor(public name: string, public age: number) {}

  greet(): string {
    return `Hello, ${this.name}`;
  }
}

export default Employee;
`);

// Get specific declarations
const interfaces = sourceFile.getInterfaces();
const classes = sourceFile.getClasses();
const functions = sourceFile.getFunctions();
const enums = sourceFile.getEnums();
const typeAliases = sourceFile.getTypeAliases();

// Get by name
const personInterface = sourceFile.getInterface("Person");
const employeeClass = sourceFile.getClass("Employee");

// Get by condition
const classWithConstructor = sourceFile.getClass(c => c.getConstructors().length > 0);
const interfaceWithTwoProps = sourceFile.getInterface(i => i.getProperties().length === 2);

// Navigate relationships
if (employeeClass) {
  // Get implements
  const implements_ = employeeClass.getImplements();

  // Get base class
  const baseClass = employeeClass.getBaseClass();

  // Get derived classes
  const derivedClasses = employeeClass.getDerivedClasses();

  // Get members
  const methods = employeeClass.getMethods();
  const properties = employeeClass.getProperties();
  const constructors = employeeClass.getConstructors();
}

// Find descendants by kind
const allIdentifiers = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.Identifier);
const allStringLiterals = sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.StringLiteral);

// Check node types
const firstClass = classes[0];
if (Node.isClassDeclaration(firstClass)) {
  // TypeScript knows this is a ClassDeclaration
  console.log(firstClass.getName());
}

// Get referencing and referenced files
const referencingFiles = sourceFile.getReferencingSourceFiles();
const referencedFiles = sourceFile.getReferencedSourceFiles();
const importStringLiterals = sourceFile.getImportStringLiterals();
```

--------------------------------

### Access Compiler Type

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/details/types.md

Retrieve the underlying compiler type from a ts-morph type object.

```typescript
const compilerType = type.compilerType;
```

Source: https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph/blob/latest/docs/setup/diagnostics.md

Get the starting character position of the diagnostic within its source file. This is a numerical offset.

const start = diagnostic.getStart(); // returns: number
```
````

<div style="border-left:3px solid #1f6feb;padding-left:14px;margin:10px 0;font-size:1.06em;line-height:1.6">

The bottleneck is concrete: compiled inner `dist/` bundles, shared-code bundles, analysis assets, and the vendored D3 runtime were admitted as JS fallbacks even though readable TypeScript exists or the file is a third-party asset. I’m enforcing source-first selection by root now: OOTB and Jimu usage scans become TS/TSX-only; SDK JS/JSX remains eligible only when no counterpart exists and it is outside asset/lib/dist trees.

</div>

````text
### Configure typescript-eslint with other plugins in flat config

Source: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/docs/packages/TypeScript_ESLint.mdx

Use this flat config setup to combine typescript-eslint with third-party plugins, enabling type-aware linting for TypeScript files while disabling it for JavaScript files.

```javascript
// @ts-check

import js from '@eslint/js';
import { defineConfig } from 'eslint/config';
import jestPlugin from 'eslint-plugin-jest';
import tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';

export default defineConfig(
  {
    // config with just ignores is the replacement for `.eslintignore`
    ignores: ['**/build/**', '**/dist/**', 'src/some/file/to/ignore.ts'],
  },
  {
    plugins: {
      '@typescript-eslint': tseslint.plugin,
      jest: jestPlugin,
    },
  },
  {
    files: ['**/*.{js,ts}'],
    extends: [js.configs.recommended],
    languageOptions: {
      parser: tseslint.parser,
      parserOptions: {
        projectService: true,
      },
    },
    rules: {
      '@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises': 'error',
      // ...
    },
  },
  {
    // disable type-aware linting on JS files
    files: ['**/*.js'],
    extends: [tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked],
  },
  {
    // enable jest rules on test files
    files: ['test/**'],
    extends: [jestPlugin.configs['flat/recommended']],
  },
);
```

--------------------------------

### Disable Type-Checked Rules in ESLint

Source: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/docs/users/Shared_Configurations.mdx

Use this configuration to disable type-aware linting on specific subsets of your codebase. It's useful when your base config includes type-aware linting but you need to conditionally turn it off using ESLint overrides.

```js
export default defineConfig(
  {
    files: ['**/*.{js,ts}'],
    extends: [js.configs.recommended, tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked],
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: {
        projectService: true,
      },
    },
  },
  // Added lines start
  {
    files: ['**/*.js'],
    extends: [tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked],
  },
  // Added lines end
);
```

```js
module.exports = {
  extends: [
    'eslint:recommended',
    'plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended-type-checked',
  ],
  parser: '@typescript-eslint',
  parserOptions: {
    projectService: true,
    __tsconfigRootDir: __dirname,
  },
  root: true,
  // Added lines start
  overrides: [
    {
      files: ['**/*.js'],
      extends: ['plugin:@typescript-eslint/disable-type-checked'],
    },
  ],
  // Added lines end
};
```

--------------------------------

### Configure project service with default project options

Source: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/packages/website/blog/2024-07-31-announcing-typescript-eslint-v8.md

Enables typed linting for out-of-project files by specifying allowDefaultProject and defaultProject properties.

```javascript
import js from '@eslint/js';
import tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';

export default tseslint.config(
  js.configs.recommended,
  ...tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked,
  {
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: {
        // Remove this line
        project: ['packages/*/tsconfig.json', 'tsconfig.eslint.json'],
        // Added lines start
        projectService: {
          allowDefaultProject: ['*.js'],
          defaultProject: 'tsconfig.json',
        },
        // Added lines end
        tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname,
      },
    },
  },
);
```

--------------------------------

### Including JavaScript Files in tsconfig.json for Project Service Linting

Source: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting/typed-linting/index.mdx

Shows how to modify the 'include' array in tsconfig.json to ensure JavaScript files are processed by the project service. This is a solution for 'file not found' errors when linting .js files with type-aware rules.

```diff
"include": [
  "src",
+ "*.js"
]
```

### How do I disable type-checked linting for a file?

Source: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting/typed-linting/index.mdx

Type-checked linting can be disabled for specific files by utilizing ESLint's configuration objects with the disable-type-checked config. An alternative method is to set parserOptions: { project: false } within an override for the files intended for exclusion from type checking.
````

All clean. Here is the review, the enhancement thinking, and what I shipped.

## What I shipped: a test harness (`npm run ai:test`)

A zero-dependency suite using Node's built-in test runner, grounded against the committed indexes. 20 tests, all passing in ~9.7s.

- `golden-queries.mjs` - the query corpus, split by prompt style
- `ai-find-queries.test.mjs` - behavioral tests that run the real `ai:find --json` CLI
- `ai-index-coverage.test.mjs` - index integrity and coverage-honesty tests
- `helpers.mjs` - shared TSV/CLI helpers

It directly covers your three prompt classes:

| Tier | Prompt style | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| Literal | `DataSourceManager`, `WidgetManager`, `SettingSection`, `JimuMapViewComponent`, `DataSourceManager#getDataSource` | Exact canonical `api_id` is the top result, not thin, has a locator |
| Semantic | `loading`, `setting` | The right component appears within top-K (capability word, not type name) |
| Conceptual | `feature layer` | Enough ranked results plus related documentation surface |
| Thin/unknown | `widgetMutableStatePropChange`, `zzznotarealapi123` | Escalation path fires instead of a confident guess |

Coverage-quality tests (the "is our map trustworthy" gate): catalog version matches `version.json`; 5 known-good identities present; exports/declarations/usage-summary all join to a real symbol (the join that powers `ai:find`); `files_parsed + files_skipped == files_seen`; every ledger file has a hash and none are wrongly excluded; unresolved stays under 5% of resolved (currently ~1.7%).

## Review of the attached future work

The readme's Future Improvements list is solid and honest. My take on priority: the highest-leverage items are **CI regeneration + freshness check** (staleness is your biggest silent-failure risk) and **golden-query regression tests** (now done). Tier 3 (scip-typescript) is worth deferring exactly as planned - your ts-morph usage graph already answers most "who uses X" questions, so Tier 3 is only justified when you need guaranteed full find-references precision.

## Additional enhancements worth considering

- **`ai:verify` freshness gate.** Tiny script comparing `api/METADATA.tsv` `exb_version` to `version.json`, exiting non-zero on drift. Pair with the new `ai:test` in CI so stale indexes fail the build.
- **Fold `ai:test` into the regeneration workflow.** The golden queries are the cheapest guard against a scoring change silently breaking a known-good lookup - run them after every `ai:index:rich`/`:usages`.
- **Confidence signal in `ai:find` output.** When a query resolves into a package whose `coverage.tsv` `files_parsed/files_seen` ratio is low, print a one-line caveat. Turns the ledger into a live trust signal rather than an audit-only artifact.
- **Typo/synonym tolerance in `scoreText`.** A small edit-distance pass (`DataSrcManager` -> `DataSourceManager`) plus a hand-curated synonym map for common concept words would meaningfully improve semantic/conceptual recall, which is where the query engine is weakest today.
- **Embeddings over just `docs/api-reference.tsv` summaries.** Not the whole tree - only the already-small curated doc summaries. That is the cheapest path to real conceptual search ("show a spinner while a query runs") without knowing an API name, and it stays inside your "locate evidence, don't duplicate source" constraint.
- **Tier 3 scoping tweak** when you resume: pilot on `jimu-core` defs only (not a widget group) first - it is the densest reference target and the fastest way to measure OOM/partial-compile risk before scaling.

On the "keep both vs switch" decision: keep both, as recommended. The new coverage tests now let you retire the regex `dist-widgets/` later with confidence, since any accuracy regression in the ts-morph path would trip the join-integrity and known-good assertions.

To run: `npm run ai:test`.

💡 I'm working through whether we can deprecate dist-widgets once dist-widgets-ts reaches feature parity in Phase E. I need to weigh the tradeoffs—the current dist-widgets uses a regex-based scanner with no dependencies that runs in about a second, so I'm considering what we'd gain or lose by consolidating to the TypeScript version.

The real issue is that parity of output files doesn't mean parity of how they're generated. The regex approach is fast, cheap, and dependency-free, while the ts-morph scanner takes 65 seconds, requires 1.4GB of heap, and adds a TypeScript dependency—so removing the regex path would force every dist-widgets lookup through that heavier build. There's also a robustness question: the regex scanner can't fail to compile, but ts-morph depends on type resolution working correctly, so version bumps or tsconfig changes could partially break the rich build.

Coverage-wise, the regex scanner captures non-exported symbols and content even when files don't typecheck, whereas ts-morph might skip or misresolve files with type errors—especially relevant for the Esri dist built in a monorepo. The freshness concern is real too: the fast index regenerates dist-widgets on every run, but if you remove regex, widget data only comes from the 65-second rich build, so staleness risk increases unless someone runs it regularly.

For jsx-usage accuracy, the ts variant would be more precise since it identifies real JSX elements, but regex still serves as a fast fallback. The bigger picture is that dist-widgets-ts exists partly as a validation harness to diff against regex dist-widgets and catch ts-morph extraction regressions—removing regex eliminates that safety check. My thinking is leaning toward keeping both: parity is about file coverage so agents don't lose data when consulting the ts folder, not about making one redundant.

But considering the case for removing it: the upside is simplicity (one folder for agents, no duplicate data, higher quality from ts), but the downside is losing the dependency-free ~1s path, forcing every widget lookup through the 65s/1.4GB rich build, losing the regex fallback when ts-morph partially fails, losing regression detection, and breaking the default `npm run ai:index` workflow. A middle ground would be keeping both as-is, or making ts authoritative only if the rich build runs in CI so it's always fresh.

Actually, there's a cleaner third option: trim the overlap by keeping regex as the fast default for structural data and reverse indexes, while ts handles only what regex can't produce—resolved types and components-props. That eliminates duplication without sacrificing the fast path. I should present this clearly since the user specifically asked whether we can remove dist-widgets and what the tradeoffs are.

But this creates a tension with Phase E: if we slim ts to just the type-accurate extras, is Phase E (bringing ts to parity) even necessary? That depends on whether we're going with strategy A—complete both folders for maximum redundancy at the cost of Phase E work and dual maintenance—or strategy B, where regex stays the complete default and ts becomes a specialized type-focused variant, making Phase E unnecessary.

Strategy C (ts-only with CI regeneration, deleting regex) feels riskier given that regex is the dependency-free default output and losing that fallback seems costly. I'm leaning toward A or B instead, and now I need to think through what's actually cleanest for an AI agent consuming this repo.

The duplicate folders do create real cognitive overhead for agents—which one do I grep?—but the router doc's guidance to prefer dist-widgets-ts when present, else dist-widgets, handles that. Good question to settle before we build Phase E, because the answer changes whether Phase E is even worth doing.

## Short answer

Technically yes, after Phase E the `dist-widgets-ts/` folder would carry the same *files*. But file parity is not property parity. The two generators differ in cost, dependencies, and failure modes, and those differences are the whole reason the regex variant exists. My recommendation is **keep `dist-widgets/`** even at parity.

## Why they are not actually equivalent

| Dimension | `dist-widgets/` (regex) | `dist-widgets-ts/` (ts-morph) |
|---|---|---|
| Build time | ~1s | ~65s |
| Memory | trivial | ~1.4 GB, needs `--max-old-space-size` |
| Dependency | none | `ts-morph` |
| Runs in | `npm run ai:index` (base, default) | `npm run ai:index:rich` (opt-in) |
| Freshness | regenerated every fast index run | only when someone runs the heavy build |
| Robustness | always emits; text never "fails to compile" | depends on the checker resolving the vendor tree; a version bump or monorepo-only build can partially misresolve |
| Sees non-typecheckable files | yes | may skip/misresolve |
| Type accuracy | guessed | resolved (its real advantage) |

## Benefits of keeping `dist-widgets/`

- **Fast, always-fresh default.** The base `ai:index` produces widget data in ~1s with no dependency. Delete it and every widget-capability lookup now requires the 65s/1.4 GB rich build to have been run recently. Staleness risk goes up, not down.
- **Dependency-free fallback.** If a future ExB bump breaks ts-morph resolution (the Esri dist is built in a monorepo and does not always compile standalone), regex still yields usable leads. You never end up with zero widget evidence.
- **A regression cross-check.** The ts folder's own README frames it as "diff against the regex variant before switching over." The regex output is the ground-truth diff target that catches silent ts-morph extraction regressions. Removing it removes that check.

## Cost of keeping it

- Two folders the agent must route between (mitigated today by the router rule "prefer `dist-widgets-ts/` when present, else `dist-widgets/`").
- Duplicated, potentially divergent data (mitigated by Phase E's shared `widget-catalog.mjs` helpers, so the reverse indexes cannot drift).

## The three real options

- **A. Parity + keep both (Phase E as planned).** Max redundancy, both folders complete. Cost: the dual maintenance you are questioning.
- **B. Keep regex as the complete fast default; slim ts to only what regex cannot do** (resolved types + `components-props.tsv`). Skip Phase E; document ts as an enrichment overlay. Least duplication, keeps the fast path, but the agent must know ts is partial.
- **C. ts-only, delete regex.** Only safe if the rich build is wired into CI so it is always regenerated, and you accept the dependency and the loss of a fallback and the diff check. Not recommended.

My rec is **B** if your priority is simplicity, or **A** if your priority is redundancy and a clean single folder to grep. I would not do **C**.

</div>

<div style="border-left:3px solid #1f6feb;padding-left:14px;margin:10px 0;font-size:1.06em;line-height:1.6">

Good question - our current `scoreText` is a hand-rolled scorer (substring + a bounded Levenshtein + a tiny abbreviation map), and `lib/semantic.mjs` is a hand-rolled TF-IDF. Both work, but they're reinventing what mature, tiny, zero/near-zero-dependency libraries already solve better. Researched on GitHub:

## Libraries found

| Library | Stars | Size | Fuzzy | Ranking | Notably |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fuse.js** | 20.4k | 6.8-8.6 kB | Bitap edit-distance | Custom scoring, **new Token Search**: BM25-style IDF weighting, per-word typo tolerance, word-order independent | Zero dependencies. Its new `useTokenSearch: true` mode is almost exactly our use case: `fuse.search('express midleware rout')` finds "Express Middleware" and "Express Routing Guide" despite typos, ranks rare terms higher. |
| **MiniSearch** | 6.1k | ~29 kB | Edit distance as a fraction of term length (`fuzzy: 0.2`) | **Real BM25** | Zero dependencies. Built-in prefix search, field boosting, and `autoSuggest()` (typo-tolerant query completion) - could replace our `--all`/`--semantic` scaffolding directly. |
| **FlexSearch** | 13.8k | varies (custom builds) | Phonetic/encoding-based (Soundex-like), not classic edit-distance | Contextual position scoring | Zero dependencies, fastest of the four, but its "fuzzy" is charset/phonetic transforms, which is a worse fit for identifier-style queries (`DataSrcManager`) than edit-distance or BM25 token matching. |
| **Orama** | 10.5k | ~2 kB core | Typo tolerance + BM25 | Also supports real **vector/hybrid search** | Core is dependency-free, but true semantic (embedding) search needs `@orama/plugin-embeddings` (`@tensorflow/tfjs-node`, 100s of MB) or a hosted API - that's a real dependency/network cost, not "better fuzzy search." |

## Recommendation

**Fuse.js Token Search or MiniSearch** would directly replace our bespoke `scoreText` + Levenshtein + abbreviation map with a properly tested BM25/typo-tolerant scorer, for a ~7-30 kB dependency. Concretely, this would let us delete our hand-rolled fuzzy tier and TF-IDF layer and get:
- Real BM25 ranking (ours is an ad-hoc score ladder).
- Per-word typo tolerance out of the box (no manual abbreviation map).
- MiniSearch's `autoSuggest()` could replace/strengthen our `--all` and `--semantic` modes.

**True semantic/conceptual search** (understanding "loading spinner" means `Loading`/`Progress` without a keyword map) genuinely requires embeddings, which means either a heavy local model (`@xenova/transformers`, ~100+ MB download) or a network API call. That's a real architecture change (dependency footprint, offline guarantee, possibly network egress from a vendor-boundary tool) - worth deciding deliberately, not bundling into a "better fuzzy search" swap.

Want me to:
1. Add MiniSearch (or Fuse.js Token Search) as a devDependency and replace our custom `scoreText`/fuzzy/TF-IDF in `ai-find.mjs` and `lib/semantic.mjs` with it, keeping the same `--json` output shape and `ai:test` fixtures passing, or
2. Just note this as a future option and leave the current zero-dependency implementation as-is?

💡 Since Fuse scores lower for better matches, I need to invert it so it combines additively with visibilityScore the same way the old scoring did, with higher meaning better. I'm thinking through how to replace scoreText by building a Fuse instance per query call against the symbols dataset, since scoreSymbols gets invoked separately for top-level and member rows.

Token search needs corpus-level stats like document frequency and field count, which a one-off comparison can't supply, so I'm building the Fuse index once over the full record set and using its search method to get matched items with scores instead of scoring row by row. I'm replacing the manual filter-and-score loop with a Fuse-based index function, then writing a scoreSymbols wrapper that runs the search and pulls more results than needed before trimming down.

I realize the old filter requiring a match beyond the visibility baseline is now redundant since Fuse only returns actual matches, so that check can be dropped. What matters is preserving the ranking hierarchy where exact matches beat fuzzy ones — Fuse's own scoring already favors exact matches near zero, so I'm inverting that score and adding a small visibility bonus as a tiebreaker to keep the same priority order as before.

I also need multi-word queries like "feature layer" to still work with default any-token matching, and I want to make sure compound-token abbreviations like "DataSrcManager" or "WidgetMgr" still get picked up through the tokenizer's fuzzy matching on letter/mark/number boundaries.

So "DataSourceManager" stays as one token, meaning fuzzy matching "DataSrcManager" against it comes down to Bitap's normalized score rather than raw edit distance, especially with ignoreLocation enabled. I should just test this empirically once implemented rather than hand-deriving the exact distance.

Given the uncertainty around thresholds for abbreviation-style mismatches like "Mgr" vs "Manager" or "Secton" vs "Section", I'm leaning toward keeping explicit abbreviation expansion as a pre-query rewriting step rather than trusting Bitap distance alone, since Bitap is really modeling typo-like closeness rather than semantic abbreviation matching.

That confirms neither Bitap nor bounded Levenshtein would catch these abbreviations, which is why I added the explicit ABBREVIATIONS map for src/mgr/cfg. I'll keep that expansion step but delegate the actual fuzzy scoring to Fuse, running it against both the original and abbreviation-expanded query and keeping whichever score is lower, building the Fuse index once per invocation over the symbol rows with token search enabled.

For scoring, I'll generate deduped query variants (original plus expanded), then for each subset of rows (top-level vs member fallback) build a fresh Fuse instance since Fuse indexes a specific array, accepting the small rebuild cost given the subsets are modest in size.

Then I'll apply the same top-level-first-then-member fallback ranking as before, capped at 12 results. I should also clean up now-unused helpers like levenshtein since Fuse replaces it, but scoreText is still used elsewhere for docs/packages/routes and semantic scoring, so I need to grep for all its call sites before removing anything.

<details class="agent-reasoning"><summary><sub><span style="color:#7d8590;font-weight:400">🧠 Agent reasoning (1 thought)</span></sub></summary>

<div style="color:grey;margin-left:2em;margin-top:8px;">

💡 Interesting — with Fuse Token Search, the query now correctly finds the exact internal symbol as a top match, something the old hand-rolled abbreviation-only scorer couldn't do since that symbol wasn't exported and was only reachable via mentions.tsv escalation before.

Checking resultIsThin(), it only flags a result as thin when docs, storybook, and behavioral usages are all zero across every result — and here the related widgetStatePropChange has 82 behavioral usages, so it's correctly not thin. This is a real improvement: Fuse's token matching resolves an internal action symbol the old ranking logic missed entirely, since the old scoreText only matched via exact/prefix checks against api_id, name, or module_path.

If widgetStatePropChange had beh=82 before too, it would've made thin=false then as well, so something else must have changed which candidates make it into the top-12 set, not just the thin check itself. I'm now reconsidering the old scoring filter — it only keeps rows whose score exceeds the baseline visibility score, meaning any genuine substring match like this one should have passed that filter in the old code too, so I need to check whether "widgetstatepropchange" actually satisfies the substring condition against the query.

Checking the actual strings: the full query is "widgetmutablestatepropchange" but the candidate text is "widgetstatepropchange" — missing "mutable" — so the substring match fails, and the fuzzy edit-distance check also fails since the gap is too large for the allowed threshold. So under the old algorithm this row would have scored zero and been excluded from the ranked results entirely.

```markdown
# Plan: AI Index Enhancements (ai:find quality + freshness)

Improve retrieval quality, trust signals, and staleness safety of the ExB evidence index. Scope = enhancement items 1, 3, 4, 5 from the prior review, informed by the user's 7 questions. Zero-dependency first; defer anything needing a model/dep.

## Answers that shape scope
- Q1 partial/case-insensitive: WORKS via scoreText `.includes()` (lowercased). Gaps: no glob (`*X*` breaks), no exhaustive "list all matches" mode (caps at top 12). -> add `--all` substring-list mode + strip wildcard chars.
- Q2 fuzzy/typo: NONE today (exact/prefix/contains/all-terms). -> item 4.
- Q3 API-to-usage coverage ratio: tests do NOT compute it. -> add metric + gate.
- Q4 semantic layer: feasible zero-dep (concept map + TF-IDF over docs summaries); embeddings deferred. -> item 5.
- Q5 coverage.tsv health in ai:find: NOT surfaced. -> item 3.
- Q6 cross-links: online doc URLs ALREADY emitted (docs + storybook canonical_url); NO skill links, NO member deep-links. -> add both.
- Q7 dist-widgets-ts is NOT a superset: missing catalog.tsv, jsx-usage.tsv, manifests.tsv, module-usage.tsv (reverse-index/capability files). -> keep both; DROP "retire dist-widgets" future item.

## Decisions (aligned with user)
- Q3: API-to-usage ratio goes into BOTH ai:verify and a test.
- Q6: add BOTH skill cross-links and member deep-links in Phase B.
- Q7: enhance build-ai-index-ts.mjs to ALSO generate the 4 indexes the regex variant has (catalog.tsv, jsx-usage.tsv, manifests.tsv, module-usage.tsv). See Phase E. Keep both variants running.
- Keep both dist-widgets variants. Remove the readme "retire dist-widgets" item.
- Removal of dist-widgets was considered and REJECTED (user chose Option A). Rationale: file parity != property parity. Regex variant is the ~1s, dependency-free, always-fresh default emitted by base `ai:index`, a fallback when ts-morph resolution partially fails (Esri dist is monorepo-built, not always standalone-compilable), and the diff cross-check for ts extraction regressions. ts variant stays the type-accurate opt-in. Phase E brings ts to FILE parity so agents consulting the ts folder do not lose catalog/jsx-usage/manifests/module-usage.
- Semantic layer = zero-dep concept map + TF-IDF over docs/api-reference.tsv summaries + packages.tsv purposes, computed at query time (3195 rows is cheap). Defer true vector embeddings unless approved.
- ai:find changes must preserve the existing --json shape (append fields, do not rename) so ai:test and downstream stay stable.
- All new scripts: /* eslint-disable */ + @ts-nocheck, validate with node --check (matches repo convention).

## Phase A - Retrieval quality in ai:find (item 4 + Q1)
File: .scripts/ai-find.mjs (scoreText, visibilityScore, parseArgs, main).
1. Add a fuzzy tier to scoreText: Levenshtein distance for terms >= 5 chars; distance 1 -> ~300, distance 2 -> ~180, ranked BELOW `contains`, ABOVE nothing. Deterministic tie-break by api_id.
2. Add local bounded levenshtein() helper (early-exit at max distance 2). No dependency.
3. Add `--all` (alias `--grep`) mode: strip `*`/glob chars, return every substring match (case-insensitive) sorted by visibility then api_id, bypassing the top-12 cap. Document in usage string.
4. Optional tiny curated synonym map (ds->DataSource, mgr->Manager) applied before scoring; commented.

## Phase B - Trust signals + cross-links in ai:find (item 3 + Q5 + Q6)
File: .scripts/ai-find.mjs (main, printText, JSON payload). Reads coverage.tsv, docs/api-reference.tsv anchors.
1. Load coverage.tsv once in main(); build owner/package -> {files_parsed, files_seen, ratio}.
2. Attach `coverageHealth` per result (package ratio + status). Text: print one-line caveat only when ratio < 0.8. JSON: always include.
3. Member deep-links: when a docs api-reference row has an `anchor`, emit `canonical_url#anchor`.
4. Skill cross-links: static package->skill map (jimu-core/jimu-arcgis/jimu-data-source/jimu-theme/jimu-layouts/jimu-for-* -> jimu-framework-apis; jimu-ui -> jimu-ui-components; widget/manifest/setting -> exb-widget-development). Print `see skill: <name>` per result; include in JSON.

## Phase C - Semantic layer (item 5 + Q4)
New: .scripts/lib/semantic.mjs (shared, zero-dep) + wire into ai-find.mjs.
1. Curated concept map: phrase/synonym -> seed terms ("loading spinner"->Loading/Progress; "dropdown"->Select/Dropdown; "map click"->JimuMapView/hitTest). Small, hand-maintained, commented.
2. TF-IDF over docs/api-reference.tsv `summary` + packages.tsv `purpose`/`key_symbols`, built at query time. Rank by cosine of concept-expanded query terms.
3. Feed into `relatedDocumentation` as a new ranked tier (source=semantic) WITHOUT displacing exact/behavioral evidence. Add `--semantic` flag to widen expansion; default conservative.
4. Out of scope now: vector embeddings, network model. Note upgrade path in spec.

## Phase D - Freshness gate + coverage ratio (item 1 + Q3)
New: .scripts/ai-verify.mjs + `npm run ai:verify`.
1. Assert api/METADATA.tsv exb_version == ArcGISExperienceBuilder/version.json exbVersion; status == complete.
2. Assert every required index file exists and is non-empty (api/*, api-usage/summary.tsv, docs/*, coverage.tsv, files.tsv, reports/*).
3. Compute API-to-usage coverage ratio: distinct api_ids in api-usage/summary.tsv with behavioral_usages>0, divided by public (documented+storybook+declared-undocumented) top-level symbols in api/symbols.tsv. Print ratio + floor gate (start ~0.30, tune after first run; measure before locking).
4. Exit non-zero on drift/missing/below-floor. For CI and pre-regeneration.

## Phase E - dist-widgets-ts parity (Q7)
Enhance build-ai-index-ts.mjs to emit catalog.tsv, jsx-usage.tsv, manifests.tsv, module-usage.tsv with headers IDENTICAL to the regex variant.
Source functions to port/share from build-ai-index.mjs: readManifest (manifests.tsv), addUsage + usageRows (reverse-index aggregation), catalog row builder (catRows), namesFromArr/propsCsv (manifest field flattening).
1. Create shared .scripts/lib/widget-catalog.mjs with pure helpers: readManifestRow(json, group, widget, path), aggregateUsageRows(map) (-> `key\tfiles\twidgets\twidget_names`), buildCatalogRows(perWidgetCounts, manifestByWidget). No fs/ts-morph coupling so both scripts import it.
2. Refactor build-ai-index.mjs to import those helpers (behavior-preserving). Verify byte-identical output by diffing the 4 regex TSVs before/after.
3. In build-ai-index-ts.mjs main()/extractFile():
   - module-usage: derive from existing out.imports (module -> set of group/widget). Skip locale/binary modules (reuse isLocaleModule/isBinaryModule already in the ts script).
   - jsx-usage: collect JSX tags via ts-morph (getDescendantsOfKind JsxOpeningElement + JsxSelfClosingElement -> tag text); aggregate tag -> widgets. This is MORE accurate than the regex tag guess.
   - manifests: separate fs walk of dist/widgets for manifest.json (project only loads .ts/.tsx), feed readManifestRow -> manifests.tsv.
   - catalog: group accumulated components/hooks/classes/symbols by group/widget; join manifest label/exbVersion/dependency -> buildCatalogRows.
4. writeTsv the 4 files into dist-widgets-ts/ with exact regex headers. Update the ts README table + counts line.
5. Parity check: same column headers; row counts within expected variance (ts jsx-usage may differ from regex by design). Update readme-ai-index.md "Redundant?" notes to reflect dist-widgets-ts now carrying these.
```

- Experience Builder runtime widgets should bind map views via JimuMapViewComponent + onActiveViewChange instead of relying only on MapViewManager.getAllJimuMapViewIds()[0].
- In this repo, useMapWidgetIds from widget settings can differ from JimuMapView internal IDs (e.g., widget_1 vs widget_1-dataSource_1), so fallback lookup should map by prefix if needed.
- For grid-overlay runtime, keep stationary watch effect dependent on jimuMapView only to avoid repeated re-registration on config changes.
- ExB 1.20 release matrix maps to ArcGIS JS API 5.0.12 and Calcite 5.0.2; version mismatches can surface as runtime failures in Table/FeatureTable.
- Repo + ExB 1.20 are both React 19. src/tsconfig.json MUST use "jsx":"react-jsx" + "jsxImportSource":"@emotion/react" (matching client tsconfig). Classic "jsx":"react" breaks under React 19 types (global JSX namespace removed) -> "Property 'div' does not exist on JSX.IntrinsicElements" / "X cannot be used as a JSX component".
- Dual @arcgis/core type identities exist: ambient __esri (jimu-arcgis) vs module types via esri/* alias. Casting `x as unknown as __esri.Basemap` does NOT resolve cross-identity assignment mismatches (e.g. view.map.basemap = new Basemap(...)); use `as any` like use-editor.ts does.
- Authoritative widget type-check (strictNullChecks:false): `cd ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client; npx tsc -p tscheck-bve.json --noEmit`. The editor/get_errors can show strictNullChecks null-assignment noise (useState<T>(null)) that the real build ignores; also get_errors can return stale diagnostics after edits — confirm with tsc.
- esri/* path alias (e.g. import Basemap from 'esri/Basemap', import * as reactiveUtils from 'esri/core/reactiveUtils') resolves to @arcgis/core and works in widgets that declare "dependency":["jimu-arcgis"] in manifest.json.

Guard with dsJson?.url before .includes('FeatureServer'). The manager's requestService() and many methods swallow errors via .catch(e=>resolve(e)); add console.error at the requestService funnel.
- branch-version-editor supports regular (non-versioned) editing fallback: if getUniqueVMSURL finds no VMS (or throws), widget.tsx sets editingMode='regular' and renders EditorHost over all editableLayers with no ServiceSelect/VersionSelect/AdvancedOptions. EditGate gates on readiness ('loading'|'blocked'|'ready') + map scale; 'blocked' (no permission / no editable layers / service error) disables Start Editing.

- EDITOR-ONLY false error `Immutable([...])` is not callable / "namespace-style import cannot be called" (TS2349): the VS Code TS server checks src/** with src/tsconfig.json (no root tsconfig; src/tsconfig.json has no `include` so it owns all of src/), which sets `esModuleInterop: true`. jimu-core/index.d.ts line 5 = `import * as Immutable from 'seamless-immutable'` (namespace import of a callable CJS export=), re-exported. Under esModuleInterop:true TS forbids CALLING a namespace import. The real build (client tsconfig, NO esModuleInterop, only allowSyntheticDefaultImports:true) keeps it callable => tscheck EXIT=0 + OOTB widgets call Immutable([...]) identically. PROVEN by adding only esModuleInterop:true to tscheck-bve.json => reproduces TS2349 on the Immutable() lines. FIX (optional, editor-only): remove `"esModuleInterop": true` from src/tsconfig.json (keep allowSyntheticDefaultImports:true) to match the build. NOTE src/tsconfig.json has `ignoreDeprecations:"6.0"` => CLI tsc 5.9.3 REJECTS it (TS5103); the editor uses a TS 6.0-line server.

Then RE-ADDED hideNonVisibleLayers too (2026-07-23): use-editor.ts isEffectivelyVisible(layer) walks node.parent ?? node.layer, false if any ancestor .visible===false; scoping effect makes a layer editable only if it's a service layer AND (!hideNonVisibleLayers || isEffectivelyVisible) else buildUneditableInfo; threaded via EditorHost prop; widget.tsx schemaScoped = schemaStepEnabled && schemaChosen && activeSchema not-''/not-ALL, passed to both EditorHost. Net: a non-ALL schema hides other-schema layers and those become non-editable => only visible (schema) layers are editable. Caveat: layers in NO schema are left untouched by applySchema, so if visible they stay editable (visibility-based, not strict id-based). FIXED (2026-07-24) empty-editor-after-schema bug: a non-ALL schema layer nested inside a GROUP that is toggled off stayed effectively-invisible => isEffectivelyVisible (walks ancestors) false => hideNonVisibleLayers dropped it => Editor panel empty (TDS worked because its parents were already visible/top-level; MGCP/MUVD lived under an off group). FIX in schema-visibility.ts applySchema: after setNodeVisibility(node,true) for a showSet layer, ALSO showAncestors(node,parents) to make every parent group visible. buildParentMap(map) builds child->parent lookup during a pre-order walk (do NOT rely on .parent — unreliable on MapImageLayer sublayers). Ordering is safe: hideSet siblings keep their own visible=false even when the shared parent is turned on (a visible group does not force children visible). captureVisibility runs BEFORE applySchema in handleSchemaConfirm so restoreVisibility on stop reverts the parents too. FIXED (2026-07-24) layer-never-shows-in-editor discrepancy (OTB Map Viewer lists the editable layer, greys template by SCALE; this widget didn't show it at all for MGCP/MUVD): ROOT CAUSE = collectEditableLayers (utils/versioning.ts) hard-skipped `if (!layerView.isLayerVisible()) continue;`. JimuLayerView.isLayerVisible() is TOGGLE-based up the tree ("if any layer in the layer tree is invisible, the layer is considered invisible" — jimu-arcgis/lib/views/layers/jimu-layer-view.d.ts:149; NOT scale — that's the @ignore isLayerVisibleForRendering()). Detection runs ONCE before the schema step, so off-by-default MGCP/MUVD layers were excluded from editableLayers/serviceLayers; the later applySchema turning them on was too late. FIX: (1) removed the isLayerVisible() skip so ALL supported+capable+in-scope layers are collected regardless of current visibility (like OTB); (2) made edit-time scoping ALWAYS-on — widget.tsx passes `hideNonVisibleLayers` (shorthand true) to both EditorHost (removed the schemaScoped const), so use-editor.ts disables (buildUneditableInfo, NOT removes) currently-non-visible layers. Net: hidden layers are disabled (Editor greys/omits their create template) but visible ones (incl. out-of-scale toggled-on, since isEffectivelyVisible checks .visible not scale — Editor then greys by scale itself) are enabled === OTB parity. Preserves old "edit visible layers only" for the non-schema case (old detection required visible too). SUPERSEDED (2026-07-27) — the always-on hideNonVisibleLayers itself became the bug: isEffectivelyVisible disabled ANY editable layer under a hidden GROUP (children of a not-visible group layer got buildUneditableInfo => dropped from Editor), and it was timing/staleness-prone (read live .visible; effect didn't re-run on visibility change). REPLACED visibility-based scoping with SCHEMA-ID-MEMBERSHIP scoping (decouples editability from visibility): schema-visibility.ts exports getSchemaShowIds(schemas,schemaName) (via new computeSchemaSets) = the showSet ids. widget.tsx memoizes editableSchemaIds = (schemaStepEnabled&&schemaChosen&&activeSchema&&!==ALL) ? getSchemaShowIds(schemaIds,activeSchema) : null, passed to both EditorHost (replaces hideNonVisibleLayers). editor-host.tsx prop editableSchemaIds?:Set<string>|null -> useEditor. use-editor.ts: removed isEffectivelyVisible; isInEditScope(layer)= !editableSchemaIds || editableSchemaIds.has(String(layer.id)); enabled if editable&&isInEditScope else buildUneditableInfo. Net: null scope (ALL / switcher off) => EVERY editable layer enabled regardless of visibility (child of hidden group SHOWS; Esri Editor greys template by scale/visibility itself, OTB-parity); non-ALL schema => only that schema's layer ids editable (restriction preserved, by id not visibility => no race). applySchema still sets visibility+showAncestors for DISPLAY. No visibility-timing dependency anymore. GROUP/PARENT CASCADE (2026-07-27): if a schema's configured id is a GROUP/parent, enable+show ALL descendants under it. schema-visibility.ts applySchema rewritten to 2-pass: collect a `toShow` Set = each showSet-matched node's ENTIRE subtree (showSubtree recursion over getChildNodes) + its ancestor chain (for(p=parents.get(node);p;p=parents.get(p))), then show toShow nodes / hide hideSet nodes NOT in toShow (show wins over other-schema hide for descendants under a shown parent). Removed standalone showAncestors (inlined). use-editor.ts isInEditScope now walks UP: `if(!editableSchemaIds)return true; node=layer; while(node){ if(editableSchemaIds.has(String(node.id)))return true; node=node.parent??node.layer } return false` — so a child whose ancestor group id is in the schema set is editable. Symmetry: applySchema cascades DOWN (visibility), isInEditScope walks UP (editability); both = "group id in schema ⇒ all descendants visible+editable". node.parent??node.layer handles group children (.parent) and map-image/subtype sublayers (.layer fallback); terminates at Map (no parent/layer). [SUPERSEDED old wrong logic below, see CORRECTION at end: isDevEdition===true or hostEnv==='dev' (off in qa/prod by default); logs a ONE-TIME console.debug hint when gated off. All MUTATING debug tools now early-return a no-op when !isDebug(): instrumentMethods/traceEvents/traceProps/waitForMethod/installConsoleRepl (debug-introspect.ts) + traceRequests/traceFetch (debug-net.ts imports isDebug from './debug-introspect'); pure read-only inspectors (describeSignature/snapshot/diffSnapshots) are UNGATED (safe, can't mutate). So an instrument call accidentally left in shipped code is inert in prod; force-enable on a deployed build via `window._isDebug = true` in console. - (2026-08-06) CORRECTION to the jimuConfig flag semantics in the item above (user-flagged, verified in ArcGISExperienceBuilder source): there is NO ExB runtime dev-vs-prod BUILD-MODE flag. webpack process.env.NODE_ENV is build-time ONLY, not inlined to the browser (used in webpack.common.js lines 84/100/509 + webpack-extensions.common.js:52 for sourcemap/minify decisions). (1) isDevEdition = ExB EDITION/flavor, baked from webpack env IS_DE (webpack.common.js:31 `const isDevEdition = process.env.IS_DE ? true : false`). ExB has 3 flavors: ArcGIS Online-hosted (isDevEdition=false, isInPortal=false) / Developer Edition (isDevEdition=true = this repo's local `npm start` runtime) / ArcGIS Enterprise-Portal-hosted (isInPortal=true, from IS_PORTAL). isDevEdition is the EDITION, NOT "am I in dev mode" - a Developer-Edition build can still be exported/deployed. (2) hostEnv:'dev'|'qa'|'prod' = which ESRI ArcGIS Online TIER the hosted app talks to: prod->www.arcgis.com, dev->devext.arcgis.com, qa->qaext.arcgis.com (verified switch in dist/jimu-core/index.js: `switch(hostEnv){case prod:www; case dev:devext; case qa:qaext}` building portalUrl+clientId, reached only when !isDevEdition). It is Esri-INTERNAL, effectively always 'prod' for real deployments, overridable in dev/qa via the ?__env__= query param; it is NOT the app author's build environment. (3) isInBuilder = running INSIDE the ExB Builder editing app (vs a published/standalone experience). CONSEQUENCE for gating: isDebug() must NOT use isDevEdition/hostEnv. Current src/libs/debug-introspect.ts isDebug() = explicit window._isDebug boolean override, else auto-on only when window.location.hostname is localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1] (local npm start at localhost:3001), off on every deployed host; opt-in on a deployed dev/QA server via window._isDebug=true in the console. Docs corrected in jimu-framework-apis/SKILL.md ('Runtime globals' section), exb-widget-development/SKILL.md (instrument section), and instructions rule 12. Also: DEV (non-production NODE_ENV) ExB builds emit inline source maps (webpack.common.js:100/509 sourceMapOption='inline-source-map'), so widget code is debuggable in-browser in dev.

- (2026-08-07) CORRECTION (user-flagged) to the Editor create-features SEQUENCE in items 38/40: the correct order is TEMPLATE-PICKER -> DRAW -> ATTRIBUTE-FORM -> (click header BACK-ARROW) -> PENDING-FEATURES LIST -> SAVE.
