- (2026-08-07) INVESTIGATION: 'attribute form not shown after draw on small screens' - is it a JSAPI Editor / ExB feature? FINDINGS (researched @arcgis/core 5.0 + OTB ExB edit widget in node_modules/dist): (1) NOT documented as a feature - CreateFeaturesWorkflow.d.ts JSDoc says the OPPOSITE: 'After the initial sketch is created, the attribute form will display with the set field elements.' No small-screen/responsive caveat. (2) The JSAPI Editor widget has NO responsive/breakpoint code: grep of node_modules/@arcgis/core/widgets/Editor.js + Editor/** + Editor/components/** for widthBreakpoint|breakpoint|responsive|matchMedia|mobile|clientWidth/Height = EMPTY. So the native Editor always creates+shows the form step after sketch; it does not hide by screen size. (3) The ONLY form-visibility flag found, alwaysShowFeatureForm, is a prop on the <arcgis-paste> map-component (copy/paste feature) in dist/widgets/common/edit editor-copy-paste.tsx - unrelated to the draw flow. (4) Our branch-version-editor + the OTB common/edit widget have no small-screen form-hiding logic. CONCLUSION (strong inference, NOT yet confirmed live): the suppression is an ExB APP-LAYOUT effect on small form factors (ExB mobile/small-screen layout via _mobilePanelManager collapses/repositions the widget's hosting panel) - the Editor still pushes the attribute-form calcite-flow-item but its panel isn't surfaced. To make it configurable WE own it (no JSAPI toggle exists): watch editor.viewModel.state/activeWorkflow (already have window.__bveEditor), detect small screen (matchMedia / container ResizeObserver / ExB small-screen signal), then either force-surface the form panel or deliberately keep the user on the pending-list - expose as a widget config (e.g. showAttributeFormOnSmallScreens). LIVE-CONFIRM CAVEAT: resizing the shared session to phone width may remount the widget and DROP pending edits - only test after pending features are saved/discarded, or in a fresh throwaway page (setViewportSize small BEFORE drawing). Baseline captured at viewport 1042x697: .esri-editor + calcite-flow 344x421 visible, widget panel 360 wide.
- (2026-08-07) CONFIRMED LIVE (resize test) the item-44 small-screen finding: at phone width ExB switches to its MOBILE LAYOUT and the EditBV widget is UNMOUNTED. Evidence: page.setViewportSize small -> window.__bveEditor became undefined, .esri-editor DOM gone, leftover calcite-flow was 0x0 / offsetParent:false; ExB moved the Section's widgets into a BOTTOM TAB BAR (tablist EditBV / Map Layers / Add Layers) + a collapsible BOTTOM SHEET (pull-up ^ 'Expand' handle) with the map fullscreen (screenshot-confirmed). So on small screens the ENTIRE Editor panel is collapsed/unmounted (not just the form) - after drawing on the fullscreen map, the attribute-form calcite-flow-item is created inside the collapsed/absent panel and never surfaced. This DEFINITIVELY confirms it is an ExB app-layout behavior, NOT a JSAPI Editor feature. GOTCHAS learned: (a) ExB small-screen breakpoint for THIS app is ~1042px app width (desktop at 1042, still mobile at 960); (b) the INTEGRATED BROWSER scales requested setViewportSize by ~0.8 (req 1360 -> actual 1088; req 400 -> 320) so request ~1.25x your target width; (c) switching layouts REMOUNTS the widget and DROPS the editing session + pending features (our 3 pending were discarded this way - user had OK'd discard) - so window.__bveEditor and .esri-editor vanish; (d) rapid resize threw transient map-components 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading z)' pageErrors + 500s (harmless). Restored to desktop (viewport ~1088 -> EditGate 'You are zoomed in close enough to edit'). CONFIGURABLE APPROACH: because the widget UNMOUNTS in mobile, any 'showAttributeFormOnSmallScreens' logic must survive remount (put detection in the widget mount path, e.g. useEffect on editContainer + matchMedia/ResizeObserver); options = (1) when the Editor reaches the form step on a small screen, auto-expand the ExB mobile bottom sheet, or (2) deliberately keep the user on the pending-list. NO JSAPI toggle exists (item 44).
- (2026-08-07) RESEARCH: can we SKIP the attribute-form after a draw (to make it configurable)? ANSWER: no built-in Editor toggle, but YES via the DOCUMENTED sketch-create event. FACTS (from @arcgis/core 5.0 .d.ts): the post-draw form is NOT a separate workflow step - CreateFeaturesWorkflowStep = awaiting-feature-creation-info | creating-features | adding-attachment | editing-attachment; the form is a SUB-STATE: activeWorkflow.createFeatureState flips 'create-new' -> 'update-pending' within the 'creating-features' step (CreateFeatureState = 'create-new'|'update-pending'). VisibleElements only toggles whole sections (createFeaturesSection, editFeaturesSection, flow, sketch, settingsMenu, snappingControls, tooltipsToggle, labelsToggle, zoomToButton, undoRedoButtons, splitButton, mergeButton) - none skips the form. HOOK: EditorViewModel/Editor emits `sketch-create` (EditorSketchCreateEvent, @since 5.0): editor.on('sketch-create', evt) where evt.detail = SketchViewModelEvents['create'] (has state 'start'|'active'|'complete'|'cancel' + graphic); also 'sketch-update'. RECIPE to skip: on evt.detail.state==='complete', requestAnimationFrame(()=> activeWorkflow.hasPreviousStep && activeWorkflow.previous()) to pop the form the Editor is about to show, returning to draw/list. The drawn feature is ALREADY pending (numPendingFeatures increments on draw) so skipping only skips attribute editing (feature keeps template defaults, still editable later from the list). Trigger ONLY off sketch-create (a real draw) - clicking an existing pending feature also enters update-pending, so do NOT key off createFeatureState alone. sketch-create/previous()/cancel() are DOCUMENTED (unlike save()). Workflow base (Workflow.d.ts) public: data, hasNextStep, hasPreviousStep, started, stepId, type, cancel(CancelWorkflowOptions), commit(), next(), previous({cancelCurrentStep}), reset(), start(). CreateFeaturesWorkflow adds: createFeatureState, data, numPendingFeatures, pendingFeatures (Collection<Graphic>), updatePendingFeature(feature) ('moves the pending feature INTO update mode' = shows the form = the inverse of skipping). Documented in editor-calcite-flow.md new section '## Skipping the attribute form after a draw'. Suggest widget config skipAttributeFormOnCreate (default false). NOT yet implemented/verified live.

- (2026-08-20) CHAT EXPORTER - two big fidelity fixes + full storage map. (1) TOOL-CALL DEDUPE (fixes wrong message/tool SEQUENCE): the journal RE-EMITS each toolInvocationSerialized as its status changes (queued->running->complete-with-output). Measured this session: 549 nodes but only 397 distinct toolCallIds, 138 ids repeated (max 4x), and a later copy can drift 150+ stream positions = it lands in a DIFFERENT turn. FIX = keep the FIRST occurrence (that IS chat display order) and MERGE later updates into it (pastTense, generatedTitle, isComplete, toolSpecificData, output, exitCode, duration, resultDetails); never append the 2nd+ copy. Tool count went 522->411 after dedupe. Validated first-occurrence order against transcripts tool.execution_start: only 18/336 inversions, and those are parallel-tool batches where execution order != display order - display order (journal first-occurrence) is what matches the chat window. (2) TERMINAL OUTPUT IS IN THE JOURNAL, not just resources: `toolSpecificData.terminalCommandOutput.text` (102 of 103 distinct terminal calls had it) + `toolSpecificData.terminalCommandState.{exitCode,duration}`. Must strip ANSI/VT (SGR, cursor, OSC-title `\u001b]...\u0007`), normalize CRLF, and drop the leading shell command-echo fragment (capture starts mid-echo, e.g. "ind -- DataSourceManager"). Also `resultDetails.output[]` entries with isText=true carry model-facing results for MCP tools + some terminal calls. Render both as collapsible fenced blocks (📟 Terminal output / 📦 Tool result); clip 24KB head+tail. Result: 105 terminal outputs + 9 tool results captured where the export previously said "not persisted". STORAGE MAP (workspaceStorage/<hash>/): chatSessions/<id>.jsonl = definitive journal; GitHub.copilot-chat/{chat-session-resources (LARGE bodies, VS Code ROTATES/EMPTIES it - do not depend on it), debug-logs/<id>/{models.json,main.jsonl}, memory-tool/memories/<base64 sessionId>/, transcripts/<id>.jsonl}. TRANSCRIPTS schema (different from journal, NO output bodies): records {id,parentId,timestamp,type,data} with type in session.start / user.message / assistant.turn_start / assistant.message / assistant.turn_end / tool.execution_start (data: toolCallId, toolName, ARGUMENTS - exact paths/lineranges/commands/queries) / tool.execution_complete (data: toolCallId, success only). Useful as an independent ORDER + ARGUMENTS cross-check.

- (2026-08-18) MUTABLE STATE (widgetMutableStatePropChange / MutableStoreManager) + vendor-search technique. SEMANTICS (proven from client/dist/jimu-core/index.js, since jimu-core ships .d.ts only - no readable impl .ts): `appActions.widgetMutableStatePropChange(widgetId, propKey)` takes NO value; its reducer ONLY does `state.setIn(['widgetsMutableStateVersion',widgetId,propKey], (prev??0)+1)` = a rerender ping. The value lives OUTSIDE redux in MutableStoreManager's plain mutable object: `updateStateValue(widgetId,propKey,value)` = lodash-set(this.state,[widgetId,...propKey.split('.')],value) THEN getAppStore().dispatch(widgetMutableStatePropChange(widgetId,propKey)). So ALWAYS call MutableStoreManager.getInstance().updateStateValue(...) (public, exported from jimu-core) - never dispatch the action yourself. GOTCHA: value is written at the SPLIT path but the version is keyed by the FULL propKey string -> updateStateValue(id,'a.b',v) bumps version key 'a.b'; an observer watching version key 'a' NEVER rerenders. Consume: runtime widget reads props.mutableStateProps.<key> (+ props.mutableStatePropsVersion); a SETTING panel reads redux `appStateInBuilder.widgetsMutableStateVersion[id][key]` as an effect dep then pulls the object cross-iframe via `window._appWindow._mutableStoreManager.getStateValue([id,key])` (OOTB dist/widgets/common/text setting.tsx:56-66 + runtime widget.tsx:197). USE FOR: non-serializable/expensive runtime objects (rich-text Editor instance, __esri.Basemap caches, web-component element refs - see arcgis/basemap-gallery runtime/basemap-utils.ts useCache) and runtime->builder-setting handoff. NOT for saved config (onSettingChange) or serializable shared state (widgetStatePropChange, which DOES take a value and writes state.widgetsState). First arg is not strictly a widgetId - jimu's built-in SetFilter data action uses updateStateValue('dataActions', `${name}.${dsId}`, ...). Types: props.d.ts mutableStateProps/mutableStatePropsVersion, state.d.ts MutableStatePropsVersion/WidgetsMutableStateVersion, mutable-store-manager.d.ts (its class JSDoc explains the whole design). SEARCH TECHNIQUE for framework internals whose behavior exists only in the minified bundle: (1) `rg` is NOT installed on this machine - use Select-String or grep_search; (2) grep_search across the WHOLE ArcGISExperienceBuilder tree TIMES OUT - always scope includePattern to a subtree (ArcGISExperienceBuilder/client/jimu-core/**) or use Get-ChildItem -Include *.ts,*.tsx | Select-String -Context; (3) client/dist/jimu-core/index.js (1.1MB) has NO .js.map, so resolve mangled names in 2 steps: grep the webpack export map `apiName:()=>MangledId` then grep `function MangledId(` and the reducer's `case ActionKeysVar.ApiName:`; (4) .ai-context/exb indexes cover DECLARATIONS (names/kinds/paths) but NOT JSDoc bodies nor code COMMENTS, so an index miss does not mean absence - fall back to raw text search of readable source (the decisive clue here was a CODE COMMENT in text/widget.tsx naming the action).

Targets: dist/jimu-core/index.js (1.10MB - THE big one: app-actions + reducers + store + ALL managers + data-source/message/session systems; this is where widgetMutableStatePropChange's reducer + MutableStoreManager were found); dist/jimu-arcgis/index.js (JimuMapView/MapViewManager/JimuLayerView); dist/jimu-data-source/index.js; dist/jimu-for-builder/{index,service,guides,templates,json-editor-setting}.js; dist/jimu-layouts/{layout-runtime,layout-builder}.js; dist/jimu-theme/index.js (+base/); dist/jimu-ui/index.js (basic comps) + dist/jimu-ui/advanced/*.js (18 per-subpath bundles: setting-components, data-source-selector, map, rich-text-editor, sql-expression-builder, expression-builder, style-setting-components, builder-components, chart, chart-engine, arcade-content-builder, dynamic-style-builder, dynamic-url-editor, coordinate-control, portal-components, resource-selector, site-components, utility-selector) + dist/jimu-ui/basic/*.js (10 lazy: color-picker, copy-button, date-picker, guide, imagecrop, item-selector, list-tree, qr-code, runtime-components, sql-expression-runtime); APP SHELLS dist/builder/index.js (Builder app) + dist/experience/index.js (runtime app) + dist/site|template|templates/; PER-WIDGET COMPILED dist/widgets/<g>/<w>/dist/{runtime/widget.js, runtime/builder-support.js, setting/setting.js, tools/} (rarely needed - the readable src/ sits right next to it). EXCLUDE AS NOISE: client/node_modules/, any chunks/ folder (jimu-ui/chunks, shared-code/chunks - unstable webpack split names), *.LICENSE.txt, translations/ + i18n/t9n/nls, assets/, dist/calcite-components/ + dist/arcgis-{map,charts,coding,portal}-components/ (vendored Esri web components, NOT jimu), and the vendored libs in dist/jimu-core (wkid.js is 4.8MB of lookup tables, plus react.js, react-dom.js, jszip.js, bowser.js, emotion.js, js.cookie.js, request.umd.min.js), client/{dist-report,scripts,webpack,__mocks__}/.
